absent: Locking, reference counting and concurrency rules for tables, chains, rules and sets are not shown.
Netlink transport details such as family identifiers, header formats and error reporting are not shown.
Runtime evaluation semantics, packet path ordering and verdict handling beyond attribute names are not shown.
Binary encoding details such as netlink attribute types, alignment and validation beyond max markers are not shown.
Ownership transfer, capability checks and generation transaction failure handling are not shown.

findings.text: The userspace interface exposes distinct netlink commands for managing packet filtering state grouped by object kind where tables and chains and rules and sets and set elements and stateful objects and flow tables each have dedicated operations alongside generation handling and tracing. Creation uses new style commands while inspection uses get style commands and ordinary removal uses del style commands with separate destroy style commands for forced cleanup and reset variants that also clear state during reads, all bounded by a final max marker. Illustrative members include NFT_MSG_NEWTABLE for table creation and NFT_MSG_TRACE for tracing and NFT_MSG_MAX as the bound.

Table and chain and rule and set lifecycles advance from creation through query to removal where a new command introduces the object and get retrieves it and del requests deletion while destroy forces teardown even when references remain. Set element and object and flow table families follow the same pattern with additional reset reads that return counters or element state and clear them atomically. Generation commands bracket transactional batches so that clients open a generation and fetch its identifier to correlate later updates.

A generic list container carries nested element payloads where an unspecified value marks absence and a single element tag holds each entry and a public max defines the valid range. Hook attachment describes where a base chain plugs into packet flow using ordering information plus device selectors plus a hook identifier, again with an unspecified tag and a public max. Each public max equals one less than its internal upper bound. Representative tags include NFTA_LIST_ELEM for list content and NFTA_HOOK_PRIORITY for ordering and NFTA_HOOK_DEVS for multi device binding, while remaining hook tags cover NFTA_HOOK_HOOKNUM for the hook identifier and NFTA_HOOK_DEV for single device selection.

Table behavior is tuned by three independent bits where NFT_TABLE_F_DORMANT marks a table inactive and NFT_TABLE_F_OWNER records userspace ownership and NFT_TABLE_F_PERSIST keeps the table after userspace exits. Dormant occupies value one and owner occupies value two and persist occupies value four, with NFT_TABLE_F_MASK covering exactly those three bits for validation.

Table descriptions carry NFTA_TABLE_OWNER for ownership and NFTA_TABLE_USERDATA for opaque bytes and NFTA_TABLE_NAME for identity and NFTA_TABLE_FLAGS for behavior and NFTA_TABLE_HANDLE for kernel reference and NFTA_TABLE_USE for reference counting and NFTA_TABLE_PAD for alignment, framed by an unspecified tag and NFTA_TABLE_MAX as the bound. Chain roles use NFT_CHAIN_BINDING for bound chains and NFT_CHAIN_BASE for hook attached chains and NFT_CHAIN_HW_OFFLOAD for accelerated chains, where base occupies bit zero and offload occupies bit one and binding occupies bit two with NFT_CHAIN_FLAGS as the combined mask.

Chain descriptions link membership and behavior through NFTA_CHAIN_USERDATA for opaque bytes and NFTA_CHAIN_ID for transaction correlation and NFTA_CHAIN_FLAGS for role bits and NFTA_CHAIN_COUNTERS for packet statistics and NFTA_CHAIN_TYPE for subsystem hint and NFTA_CHAIN_POLICY for default verdict and NFTA_CHAIN_HOOK for hook binding and NFTA_CHAIN_NAME for identity and NFTA_CHAIN_TABLE for parent table and NFTA_CHAIN_HANDLE for kernel reference and NFTA_CHAIN_USE for reference counting and NFTA_CHAIN_PAD for alignment, bounded by NFTA_CHAIN_MAX.

Rule descriptions identify placement through NFTA_RULE_CHAIN_ID for chain correlation and NFTA_RULE_POSITION_ID for relative placement and NFTA_RULE_ID for transaction identity and NFTA_RULE_PAD for alignment and NFTA_RULE_USERDATA for opaque bytes and NFTA_RULE_POSITION for numeric order and NFTA_RULE_COMPAT for legacy matching and NFTA_RULE_EXPRESSIONS for the action list and NFTA_RULE_HANDLE for kernel reference and NFTA_RULE_CHAIN for parent chain and NFTA_RULE_TABLE for parent table, bounded by NFTA_RULE_MAX.

Compatibility matching for legacy rules carries a protocol number plus flag bits where an invert bit requests negation and an unused bit is reserved. The unused bit occupies bit zero and the invert bit occupies bit one, while the valid mask covers only the invert bit. Representative tags include NFTA_RULE_COMPAT_PROTO for the protocol and NFTA_RULE_COMPAT_FLAGS for the bits, with NFT_RULE_COMPAT_F_INV as the invert bit and NFT_RULE_COMPAT_F_UNUSED as the reserved bit and NFT_RULE_COMPAT_F_MASK as the validation mask.

Set behavior selects among storage and evaluation modes where NFT_SET_EXPR marks expression based sets and NFT_SET_CONCAT marks concatenated keys and NFT_SET_OBJECT marks object storage and NFT_SET_EVAL marks immediate evaluation and NFT_SET_TIMEOUT marks expiring entries and NFT_SET_MAP marks dictionaries and NFT_SET_INTERVAL marks ranges and NFT_SET_CONSTANT marks immutable content and NFT_SET_ANONYMOUS marks temporary sets. Values run from one for anonymous and two for constant and four for interval through eight and sixteen and thirty two and sixty four and one hundred twenty eight up to two hundred fifty six for expression sets. Allocation tuning chooses NFT_SET_POL_PERFORMANCE for speed versus NFT_SET_POL_MEMORY for compactness.

Set sizing hints describe expected entry counts plus concatenation layout, while field descriptors describe element widths. Tags include NFTA_SET_DESC_SIZE for capacity and NFTA_SET_DESC_CONCAT for packed key layout and NFTA_SET_FIELD_LEN for byte length, each family framed by an unspecified tag and bounded by NFTA_SET_DESC_MAX and NFTA_SET_FIELD_MAX respectively.

Set definitions combine identity plus typing plus lifetime plus bookkeeping through NFTA_SET_COUNT for occupancy and NFTA_SET_TYPE for backend selection and NFTA_SET_EXPRESSIONS for program lists and NFTA_SET_EXPR for single programs and NFTA_SET_HANDLE for kernel reference and NFTA_SET_OBJ_TYPE for object kind and NFTA_SET_PAD for alignment and NFTA_SET_USERDATA for opaque bytes and NFTA_SET_GC_INTERVAL for cleanup period and NFTA_SET_TIMEOUT for default expiry and NFTA_SET_ID for transaction correlation and NFTA_SET_DESC for sizing and NFTA_SET_POLICY for tuning and NFTA_SET_DATA_LEN for value width and NFTA_SET_DATA_TYPE for value kind and NFTA_SET_KEY_LEN for key width and NFTA_SET_KEY_TYPE for key kind and NFTA_SET_FLAGS for behavior and NFTA_SET_NAME for identity and NFTA_SET_TABLE for parent table, bounded by NFTA_SET_MAX.

Set elements carry key material plus optional value material with lifetime and program hooks where NFTA_SET_ELEM_EXPRESSIONS holds program lists and NFTA_SET_ELEM_KEY_END closes ranges and NFTA_SET_ELEM_OBJREF links objects and NFTA_SET_ELEM_PAD aligns and NFTA_SET_ELEM_EXPR holds a single program and NFTA_SET_ELEM_USERDATA holds opaque bytes and NFTA_SET_ELEM_EXPIRATION reports expiry and NFTA_SET_ELEM_TIMEOUT sets lifetime and NFTA_SET_ELEM_FLAGS carries status and NFTA_SET_ELEM_DATA holds values and NFTA_SET_ELEM_KEY holds keys, bounded by NFTA_SET_ELEM_MAX. Element status uses NFT_SET_ELEM_CATCHALL for wildcard entries with value two and NFT_SET_ELEM_INTERVAL_END for range terminators with value one.

Batched element operations scope a payload to one set through NFTA_SET_ELEM_LIST_SET_ID for transaction correlation and NFTA_SET_ELEM_LIST_ELEMENTS for the batched entries and NFTA_SET_ELEM_LIST_SET for the set name and NFTA_SET_ELEM_LIST_TABLE for the parent table, bounded by NFTA_SET_ELEM_LIST_MAX.

Rule data distinguishes plain values from verdicts by reserving high bits where the value kind uses zero and the verdict kind uses a high pattern with low eight clear namely 0xffffff00 and a reserved mask isolates those high bits. Payloads select either inline bytes or a verdict structure, with inline values capped at sixty four bytes. Tags include NFTA_DATA_VERDICT for verdicts and NFTA_DATA_VALUE for bytes bounded by NFTA_DATA_MAX, with NFT_DATA_VALUE as the value discriminator and NFT_DATA_VERDICT as the verdict discriminator and NFT_DATA_RESERVED_MASK as the mask and NFT_DATA_VALUE_MAXLEN as the length cap.

Verdicts encode control flow through NFTA_VERDICT_CHAIN_ID for transaction linkage and NFTA_VERDICT_CHAIN for jump targets and NFTA_VERDICT_CODE for the action, bounded by NFTA_VERDICT_MAX. Generic expressions name their implementation via NFTA_EXPR_DATA for parameters and NFTA_EXPR_NAME for kind, bounded by NFTA_EXPR_MAX. Immediate data moves copy constants via NFTA_IMMEDIATE_DATA for bytes and NFTA_IMMEDIATE_DREG for the destination register, bounded by NFTA_IMMEDIATE_MAX.

Bitwise operations support masking with xor plus shifts and logical combination where NFT_BITWISE_XOR and NFT_BITWISE_OR and NFT_BITWISE_AND cover logic and NFT_BITWISE_RSHIFT and NFT_BITWISE_LSHIFT cover shifts and NFT_BITWISE_MASK_XOR covers combined mask xor, with NFT_BITWISE_BOOL aliasing the combined form for boolean evaluation. Operands describe NFTA_BITWISE_SREG2 for a second source and NFTA_BITWISE_DATA for inline bytes and NFTA_BITWISE_OP for the selector and NFTA_BITWISE_XOR for xor bits and NFTA_BITWISE_MASK for mask bits and NFTA_BITWISE_LEN for width and NFTA_BITWISE_DREG for destination and NFTA_BITWISE_SREG for source, bounded by NFTA_BITWISE_MAX.

Byte order conversion swaps between host and network forms using NFT_BYTEORDER_HTON and NFT_BYTEORDER_NTOH with operands NFTA_BYTEORDER_SIZE for unit size and NFTA_BYTEORDER_LEN for length and NFTA_BYTEORDER_OP for direction and NFTA_BYTEORDER_DREG for destination and NFTA_BYTEORDER_SREG for source. Comparisons test NFT_CMP_GTE and NFT_CMP_GT and NFT_CMP_LTE and NFT_CMP_LT and NFT_CMP_NEQ and NFT_CMP_EQ with NFTA_CMP_DATA for the constant and NFTA_CMP_OP for the operator and NFTA_CMP_SREG for the source. Range checks use NFT_RANGE_NEQ and NFT_RANGE_EQ with NFTA_RANGE_TO_DATA for the upper bound and NFTA_RANGE_FROM_DATA for the lower bound and NFTA_RANGE_OP and NFTA_RANGE_SREG. Set match inversion uses NFT_LOOKUP_F_INV occupying bit zero. Each family is bounded by NFTA_RANGE_MAX and NFTA_CMP_MAX and NFTA_BYTEORDER_MAX respectively.

Set lookups bind NFTA_LOOKUP_FLAGS for options and NFTA_LOOKUP_SET_ID for transaction linkage and NFTA_LOOKUP_DREG for results and NFTA_LOOKUP_SREG for keys and NFTA_LOOKUP_SET for the target, bounded by NFTA_LOOKUP_MAX. Dynamic updates choose NFT_DYNSET_OP_DELETE versus NFT_DYNSET_OP_UPDATE versus NFT_DYNSET_OP_ADD with modifier NFT_DYNSET_F_EXPR for program driven data occupying bit one and NFT_DYNSET_F_INV for inversion occupying bit zero. Update parameters carry NFTA_DYNSET_EXPRESSIONS for programs and NFTA_DYNSET_FLAGS and NFTA_DYNSET_PAD and NFTA_DYNSET_EXPR and NFTA_DYNSET_TIMEOUT and NFTA_DYNSET_SREG_DATA and NFTA_DYNSET_SREG_KEY and NFTA_DYNSET_OP and NFTA_DYNSET_SET_ID and NFTA_DYNSET_SET_NAME, bounded by NFTA_DYNSET_MAX.

Payload addressing selects NFT_PAYLOAD_TUN_HEADER for tunnels and NFT_PAYLOAD_INNER_HEADER for encapsulated packets and NFT_PAYLOAD_TRANSPORT_HEADER for layer four and NFT_PAYLOAD_NETWORK_HEADER for layer three and NFT_PAYLOAD_LL_HEADER for link layer. Checksum handling offers NFT_PAYLOAD_CSUM_SCTP and NFT_PAYLOAD_CSUM_INET and NFT_PAYLOAD_CSUM_NONE with NFT_PAYLOAD_L4CSUM_PSEUDOHDR for pseudo header inclusion occupying bit zero. Tunnel parsing distinguishes NFT_INNER_GENEVE and NFT_INNER_VXLAN from NFT_INNER_UNSPEC, with header selection bits NFT_INNER_TH for transport and NFT_INNER_NH for network and NFT_INNER_LL for link and NFT_INNER_HDRSIZE for size, combined in NFT_INNER_MASK. Inner parameters carry NFTA_INNER_EXPR and NFTA_INNER_HDRSIZE and NFTA_INNER_FLAGS and NFTA_INNER_TYPE and NFTA_INNER_NUM, bounded by NFTA_INNER_MAX.

Payload access moves header bytes between packet and registers using NFTA_PAYLOAD_CSUM_FLAGS for checksum options and NFTA_PAYLOAD_CSUM_OFFSET for checksum position and NFTA_PAYLOAD_CSUM_TYPE for algorithm and NFTA_PAYLOAD_SREG for store sources and NFTA_PAYLOAD_LEN for width and NFTA_PAYLOAD_OFFSET for position and NFTA_PAYLOAD_BASE for header selector and NFTA_PAYLOAD_DREG for load destination, bounded by NFTA_PAYLOAD_MAX. Extension presence testing uses NFT_EXTHDR_F_PRESENT occupying bit zero.

Extension header operations target NFT_EXTHDR_OP_DCCP and NFT_EXTHDR_OP_SCTP and NFT_EXTHDR_OP_IPV4 and NFT_EXTHDR_OP_TCPOPT and NFT_EXTHDR_OP_IPV6, bounded by NFT_EXTHDR_OP_MAX. Field access carries NFTA_EXTHDR_SREG for store sources and NFTA_EXTHDR_OP for the protocol selector and NFTA_EXTHDR_FLAGS for options and NFTA_EXTHDR_LEN for width and NFTA_EXTHDR_OFFSET for position and NFTA_EXTHDR_TYPE for field kind and NFTA_EXTHDR_DREG for load destination, bounded by NFTA_EXTHDR_MAX.

Core packet metadata covers NFT_META_L4PROTO for layer four protocol and NFT_META_NFPROTO for family and NFT_META_SECMARK for security label and NFT_META_RTCLASSID for routing class and NFT_META_NFTRACE for tracing and NFT_META_SKGID for socket group and NFT_META_SKUID for socket user and NFT_META_OIFTYPE for output type and NFT_META_IFTYPE for input type and NFT_META_OIFNAME for output name and NFT_META_IIFNAME for input name and NFT_META_OIF for output index and NFT_META_IIF for input index and NFT_META_MARK for packet mark and NFT_META_PRIORITY for priority and NFT_META_PROTOCOL for ethertype and NFT_META_LEN for length.

Extended metadata adds bridge plus system plus time inputs through NFT_META_BRI_IIFHWADDR for bridge hardware address and NFT_META_BRI_BROUTE for rerouting and NFT_META_SDIFNAME for slave name and NFT_META_SDIF for slave index and NFT_META_TIME_HOUR for hour and NFT_META_TIME_DAY for day and NFT_META_TIME_NS for nanoseconds and NFT_META_BRI_IIFVPROTO for vlan protocol and NFT_META_BRI_IIFPVID for vlan id and NFT_META_OIFKIND for output kind and NFT_META_IIFKIND for input kind and NFT_META_SECPATH for security path and NFT_META_PRANDOM for randomness and NFT_META_CGROUP for control group and NFT_META_OIFGROUP for output group and NFT_META_IIFGROUP for input group and NFT_META_CPU for processor and NFT_META_PKTTYPE for packet type and NFT_META_BRI_OIFNAME for bridge output and NFT_META_BRI_IIFNAME for bridge input, with NFT_META_IIFTYPE aliasing input interface type for compatibility.

Routing lookups expose NFT_RT_XFRM for transform state and NFT_RT_TCPMSS for segment size and NFT_RT_NEXTHOP6 for ipv6 gateway and NFT_RT_NEXTHOP4 for ipv4 gateway and NFT_RT_CLASSID for traffic class, bounded by NFT_RT_MAX. Hashing selects NFT_HASH_SYM for symmetric versus NFT_HASH_JENKINS for general purpose, with parameters NFTA_HASH_SET_ID and NFTA_HASH_SET_NAME retained only for compatibility plus NFTA_HASH_TYPE and NFTA_HASH_OFFSET and NFTA_HASH_SEED and NFTA_HASH_MODULUS and NFTA_HASH_LEN and NFTA_HASH_DREG and NFTA_HASH_SREG, bounded by NFTA_HASH_MAX.

Metadata moves use NFTA_META_SREG for store sources and NFTA_META_KEY for selector and NFTA_META_DREG for load destination, bounded by NFTA_META_MAX. Routing moves use NFTA_RT_KEY and NFTA_RT_DREG, bounded by NFTA_RT_MAX. Socket lookups use NFTA_SOCKET_LEVEL for ancillary level and NFTA_SOCKET_DREG for destination and NFTA_SOCKET_KEY for selector, bounded by NFTA_SOCKET_MAX, selecting among NFT_SOCKET_CGROUPV2 for cgroup and NFT_SOCKET_WILDCARD for wildcard and NFT_SOCKET_MARK for mark and NFT_SOCKET_TRANSPARENT for transparency, bounded by NFT_SOCKET_MAX.

Connection tracking selectors run through NFT_CT_ID for correlation and NFT_CT_DST_IP6 and NFT_CT_SRC_IP6 for ipv6 peers and NFT_CT_DST_IP and NFT_CT_SRC_IP for ipv4 peers and NFT_CT_EVENTMASK for events and NFT_CT_ZONE for zones and NFT_CT_AVGPKT and NFT_CT_BYTES and NFT_CT_PKTS for counters and NFT_CT_LABELS for labels and NFT_CT_PROTO_DST and NFT_CT_PROTO_SRC for ports and NFT_CT_PROTOCOL for protocol and NFT_CT_DST and NFT_CT_SRC for addresses and NFT_CT_L3PROTOCOL for family and NFT_CT_HELPER for helpers and NFT_CT_EXPIRATION for lifetime and NFT_CT_SECMARK and NFT_CT_MARK for marks and NFT_CT_STATUS and NFT_CT_DIRECTION and NFT_CT_STATE for lifecycle, bounded by NFT_CT_MAX. Access uses NFTA_CT_SREG and NFTA_CT_DIRECTION and NFTA_CT_KEY and NFTA_CT_DREG, bounded by NFTA_CT_MAX.

Flow offload binds a rule to NFTA_FLOW_TABLE_NAME for the table, bounded by NFTA_FLOW_MAX. Rate limiting measures NFT_LIMIT_PKT_BYTES for bytes versus NFT_LIMIT_PKTS for packets with NFT_LIMIT_F_INV for inversion occupying bit zero, tuned by NFTA_LIMIT_PAD and NFTA_LIMIT_FLAGS and NFTA_LIMIT_TYPE and NFTA_LIMIT_BURST and NFTA_LIMIT_UNIT and NFTA_LIMIT_RATE, bounded by NFTA_LIMIT_MAX. Connection limiting counts NFTA_CONNLIMIT_FLAGS and NFTA_CONNLIMIT_COUNT with NFT_CONNLIMIT_F_INV for inversion occupying bit zero, bounded by NFTA_CONNLIMIT_MAX.

Counters report NFTA_COUNTER_PAD for alignment and NFTA_COUNTER_PACKETS for packet totals and NFTA_COUNTER_BYTES for byte totals, bounded by NFTA_COUNTER_MAX. Recency tracking uses NFTA_LAST_PAD and NFTA_LAST_MSECS for elapsed time and NFTA_LAST_SET for enablement, bounded by NFTA_LAST_MAX.

Logging selects delivery via NFTA_LOG_FLAGS and NFTA_LOG_LEVEL and NFTA_LOG_QTHRESHOLD and NFTA_LOG_SNAPLEN and NFTA_LOG_PREFIX and NFTA_LOG_GROUP, bounded by NFTA_LOG_MAX. Severity runs from most verbose NFT_LOGLEVEL_AUDIT and NFT_LOGLEVEL_DEBUG and NFT_LOGLEVEL_INFO and NFT_LOGLEVEL_NOTICE and NFT_LOGLEVEL_WARNING through NFT_LOGLEVEL_ERR and NFT_LOGLEVEL_CRIT and NFT_LOGLEVEL_ALERT down to NFT_LOGLEVEL_EMERG, bounded by NFT_LOGLEVEL_MAX.

Userspace queuing steers via NFTA_QUEUE_SREG_QNUM for dynamic numbers and NFTA_QUEUE_FLAGS for options and NFTA_QUEUE_TOTAL for fanout size and NFTA_QUEUE_NUM for queue id, bounded by NFTA_QUEUE_MAX. Queue options use NFT_QUEUE_FLAG_CPU_FANOUT for local cpu with value two and NFT_QUEUE_FLAG_BYPASS for fail open with value one, combined in NFT_QUEUE_FLAG_MASK covering value three. Quotas track NFTA_QUOTA_CONSUMED for usage and NFTA_QUOTA_PAD and NFTA_QUOTA_FLAGS and NFTA_QUOTA_BYTES for limits, bounded by NFTA_QUOTA_MAX, with NFT_QUOTA_F_DEPLETED for exhaustion occupying bit one and NFT_QUOTA_F_INV for inversion occupying bit zero.
Security marking carries a single context blob via NFTA_SECMARK_CTX, bounded by NFTA_SECMARK_MAX, with context length capped at four thousand ninety six bytes per NFT_SECMARK_CTX_MAXLEN.

Rejection chooses NFT_REJECT_ICMPX_UNREACH for extended icmp and NFT_REJECT_TCP_RST for tcp reset and NFT_REJECT_ICMP_UNREACH for icmp, with extended codes NFT_REJECT_ICMPX_ADMIN_PROHIBITED for policy and NFT_REJECT_ICMPX_HOST_UNREACH for host and NFT_REJECT_ICMPX_PORT_UNREACH for port and NFT_REJECT_ICMPX_NO_ROUTE for routing starting at zero, bounded by NFT_REJECT_ICMPX_MAX. Parameters use NFTA_REJECT_ICMP_CODE and NFTA_REJECT_TYPE, bounded by NFTA_REJECT_MAX. Address translation selects NFT_NAT_DNAT for destination versus NFT_NAT_SNAT for source, parameterized by NFTA_NAT_FLAGS and NFTA_NAT_REG_PROTO_MAX and NFTA_NAT_REG_PROTO_MIN and NFTA_NAT_REG_ADDR_MAX and NFTA_NAT_REG_ADDR_MIN and NFTA_NAT_FAMILY and NFTA_NAT_TYPE, bounded by NFTA_NAT_MAX.

Transparent proxying uses NFTA_TPROXY_REG_PORT for port and NFTA_TPROXY_REG_ADDR for address and NFTA_TPROXY_FAMILY for family, bounded by NFTA_TPROXY_MAX. Masquerade uses NFTA_MASQ_REG_PROTO_MAX and NFTA_MASQ_REG_PROTO_MIN for port range and NFTA_MASQ_FLAGS, bounded by NFTA_MASQ_MAX. Redirect uses NFTA_REDIR_FLAGS and NFTA_REDIR_REG_PROTO_MAX and NFTA_REDIR_REG_PROTO_MIN, bounded by NFTA_REDIR_MAX. Duplication uses NFTA_DUP_SREG_DEV for device and NFTA_DUP_SREG_ADDR for address, bounded by NFTA_DUP_MAX. Forwarding uses NFTA_FWD_NFPROTO for family and NFTA_FWD_SREG_ADDR for address and NFTA_FWD_SREG_DEV for device, bounded by NFTA_FWD_MAX.

Object references select either immediate use via NFTA_OBJREF_SET_ID and NFTA_OBJREF_SET_NAME for set linkage and NFTA_OBJREF_SET_SREG for key source and NFTA_OBJREF_IMM_NAME and NFTA_OBJREF_IMM_TYPE for direct naming, bounded by NFTA_OBJREF_MAX. Generation tracking reports NFTA_GEN_PROC_NAME for the owner process and NFTA_GEN_PROC_PID for its identifier and NFTA_GEN_ID for the transaction, bounded by NFTA_GEN_MAX.

Every attribute family starts with an unspecified tag marking absence and ends with an internal upper bound while exposing a public max exactly one less for range checks. Flag groups use distinct low bits with combined masks for validation, and transaction correlation relies on separate numeric identifiers plus handles that remain stable across get and del operations.

Several compatibilities require care where a boolean alias reuses the combined mask xor operation and an input type alias duplicates another tag and two hash set tags remain only as deprecated placeholders. Masks that combine valid bits must be used for validation rather than assuming all bits, and reserved high bits separate verdicts from values so callers must mask before interpreting payloads. Length caps on inline values and security contexts bound userspace input.

The header exports a stable userspace contract for nftables control covering netlink commands plus per object attribute dictionaries plus expression parameters plus flag and mask constants. Downstream code can rely on tag presence and max bounds for forward compatibility while treating unknown tags as ignorable and validating flags against the published masks.
